parsed.why: Strong state protections: public-accommodation nondiscrimination, hate-crime reporting, shield law, self-declared state documents. Unrepealed sodomy statute is unenforceable. National border, passport and custody exposures remain, capping the score.

Comprehensive protections, sanctuary law, strong law score, but two trans women shot in ten weeks in one city with no denominator; documented local violence offsets some of the protective regime. National exposures remain.

Worst-policy tier: bathroom misdemeanour, care ban, no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime protection, X markers rescinded, religious refusal law. State-imposed universal exposures add to hostile national framework.

Hostile statutes enacted but repeatedly blocked by state courts applying constitutional dignity and equal protection; facilities ban restrained, care ban struck down. Court record works for trans people, partly offsetting enacted restrictions and national framework.

Local law protective and ranked low-risk, but national legislature directly attached a facilities ban and can override local protections; protest arrests show enforcement. National framework applies directly, slightly below parent.
